questions.prompt: Lines ℓ and m are parallel and are cut by transversal t, crossing ℓ at P and m at Q. Explain, using a translation, why corresponding angles ∠1 and ∠5 are congruent.
questions.prompt_markup: Lines ℓ and m are parallel and are cut by transversal t, crossing ℓ at P and m at Q. Explain, using a translation, why corresponding angles ∠1 and ∠5 are congruent.
questions.correct_answer: The translation that moves Q to P maps m onto ℓ and maps t onto itself, so it maps ∠5 onto ∠1; translations keep angle measure.
questions.required_method: Translate along the transversal from Q to P. Explain why the image of m is ℓ and why the image of ∠5 is ∠1.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: (1) the translation maps t onto itself (it moves along t); (2) it maps m to a line through P parallel to m; (3) by the parallel postulate that line is ℓ; (4) so the angle formed by t and m at Q maps to the corresponding angle at P; (5) angle measure is kept.

questions.skill: Prove the converse: congruent alternate interior angles make lines parallel
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Lines ℓ and m are cut by transversal t, and alternate interior angles ∠3 and ∠5 are congruent. Prove that ℓ ∥ m.
questions.prompt_markup: Lines ℓ and m are cut by transversal t, and alternate interior angles ∠3 and ∠5 are congruent. Prove that ℓ ∥ m.
questions.required_method: Indirect proof: suppose ℓ and m meet; they would form a triangle with t whose angles contradict a known result. Or use the 180° rotation about the midpoint of PQ.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential (indirect): if ℓ and m met at a point R, triangle PQR would have an exterior angle equal to a remote interior angle, which is impossible (an exterior angle is greater than each remote interior angle); so they do not meet. Alternative: the 180° rotation about the midpoint of PQ swaps P and Q and maps ℓ onto m, so if they met on one side they would also meet on the other, giving two common points. Invalid: assuming ℓ ∥ m.
